We need to build an HTML game (no package.json → 'html' type, served statically). Three.js could be loaded via CDN but that's risky offline? The environment has network probably. Better to vendor three.js locally via npm install into a vendor folder? We can't have package.json (unsupported unless vite). We could just create package.json with vite, but then start.sh runs npm ci/install and vite build. Simpler: plain index.html + ES modules with three.js bundled locally. We can download three.module.js from CDN into `vendor/three.module.js` and use importmap. That gives offline reliability.

Let's check network access.

Plan: Build a polished GTA-style 3D open world driving game with police chase:
- Three.js scene, procedural city grid with buildings, roads, sidewalks, streetlights, trees, park.
- Player drives a car (third-person chase camera), WASD/arrow controls, handbrake, boost maybe.
- Police AI: cop cars spawn, pursue player, ramming, wanted level stars (1-5), escalation, wanted meter decays when out of sight.
- Traffic: civilian cars driving on roads, pedestrians walking, collisions.
- HUD: speedometer, minimap with roads/blips, wanted stars, health, timer, money, objective "Survive the chase".
- Mobile touch controls: virtual joystick + pedals, responsive.
- Sound: WebAudio engine hum, siren, crash impacts, generated procedurally (no assets).
- Pause, restart, start screen.

This is a big build. Need to be careful about quality and performance, and verify with playwright screenshot.

I should consider using the gauntlet-loop skill? The user just gave a goal. The available skill "gauntlet-loop" turns goal into a prompt — not needed since we're the agent doing it. Just build.

Let me set a quality bar myself: looks good in screenshots, runs at good fps, gameplay functional.

Design details:

World: city grid 5x5 blocks, block size ~90 with road width 14. Roads along x and z. Buildings random heights 15-70 with emissive windows. Use instanced meshes for buildings? For simplicity use merged geometry or instancing with per-instance colors. Windows via canvas texture per building type—maybe generate a facade texture with lit windows and use per-instance color? Instanced meshes share material; can use instanceColor. Texture with windows via canvas repeated. That would look decent.

Alternative: create ~80 buildings with BoxGeometry and a shared material array? Windows need texture. Use canvas-generated facade texture (dark building with lit windows grid), repeated according to building scale. If using individual meshes with material clones per building for repeat, that's ~80 draw calls, fine.

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)

## Objective
- Build a polished browser-based 3D open-world driving game in the style of GTA, featuring police chases, for the previously empty `PlayGround` repo.

## Requirements
- 3D open world, GTA-style city, police pursuit gameplay.
- Must run in browser via existing static `start.sh` / default server setup.
- Support desktop and mobile (responsive HUD, touch controls).
- Keep the project self-contained; Three.js is vendored locally.
- (User gave no further explicit constraints.)

## Decisions
- Plain HTML/CSS/ES modules, no bundler; Three.js r169 vendored at `vendor/three.module.js` with import map.
- Night neon city built procedurally: merged building geometry, emissive window texture, roads, sidewalks, parks, streetlights, signs, skyline.
- Arcade car physics with drift/handbrake/nitro, third-person chase camera.
- Police AI navigates road grid, ramming, wanted/heat escalation, helicopter at 3+ stars.
- Procedural WebAudio (engine, siren, crashes, pickups) with no external assets.
- Vendored `three.module.js` downloaded from unpkg.

## Work State
### Completed
- Full project scaffold: `index.html`, `styles.css`, `src/*.js` modules.
- Procedural city world, player car, physics, collisions, traffic, pedestrians, police manager, helicopter, particles/skids, HUD/minimap/speedometer, start/pause/game-over screens, mobile touch controls, audio.
- Vendored Three.js and Playwright Chromium installed for testing.
- Verified desktop menu and gameplay screenshots via Playwright; no JS errors, only SwiftShader GPU performance warnings.
- Several visual fixes: brighter buildings/streetlight pools, neon storefronts, soft underglow/headlight cone, gold wanted stars, visible cops at start, removed speedometer MAX label.

### Active
- Final visual/gameplay tuning and verification after last edits.

### Blocked
- None.

## Next Move
1. Test the latest start-position/menu-camera changes (start moved to `CITY.start = (0, 0, -16)`) with screenshots.
2. Run a driving/police logic test at a small viewport (e.g. 640x480) holding `w`, verifying speed, collisions, wanted escalation, game over.
3. Test mobile viewport (390x844) standalone (do not run desktop and mobile pages simultaneously; that caused screenshot timeouts).
4. Test default capture (`capture.sh` with `CAPTURE_URL` / `CAPTURE_DIR`) or playwright-cli screenshots.
5. Clean up unused imports/vars, update README if desired, and commit final changes.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js`: game loop, state, camera, player, scoring, pickups, debug hooks.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js`: city generation, buildings, roads, lights, parks, skyline.
